author: project-history-agent
title: /experiments delivered: tasks, topic notes, reports, timeline and questions, newest first
body:
What was built (journal, server/done, 08:29Z):

- **Store:** append-only topic notes (`lib/notes.mjs`, `tools/notes.mjs add|list|topics|validate`, `status/topics.json` with 13 topics, `status/notes/<topic>.jsonl`); duplicate ids and unknown `supersedes` are refused; corrections supersede. Task records (`lib/tasks.mjs`, `status/tasks.json`: 15 tasks and the current phase), each with an Owner and an Agents side.
- **Pages** (`server/history.mjs`, `server/pages/history.mjs`, safe Markdown in `server/markdown.mjs`): `/experiments` index, `/experiments/<id>` per task or experiment, `/experiments/topics`, `/experiments/topic/<id>` with kind/author filters and supersede chains, `/experiments/reports` and `/experiments/report?path=` (read-only; only `eval/reports/current` and `eval/reports/history`; `..`, absolute paths, NUL, backslashes and symlink escapes refused), `/experiments/timeline` (the former status page), `/experiments/questions`; JSON under `/experiments/api/*`. `/project` paths answer 301; `/project/api/*` stays as an alias. Former DS ids in old links resolve through `docs/specs/aliases.json`.
- **Seeded history:** 99 notes from the journal, the experiment registry, questions.md and the reports, with sources linked; owner decisions attributed to the owner.
- **Checks:** `npm test` 585/585 (new `tests/notes.test.mjs`, `tests/experiments-pages.test.mjs`), `check-spec-refs` 0 violations, `site-menu --check` ok, `check-links` 0 broken (711 pages); live check on port 9471 with scratch state and headless Chromium screenshots (desktop and phone), server stopped afterwards.

Known limits: task pages relate notes and journal events by `match` phrases, so a page can show a loosely related event; seeded notes carry the time of their source event, not the time they were written; notes are only as current as agents keep them.

author: claude-agent
title: Chat model selector, on-demand CPU formalizers and a three-way language choice
body: The chat no longer depends on an external formalizer.url. config/formalizers.json lists SmolLM2-135M (fastest), Gemma 3 270M, SmolLM2-360M (best English OOD, default) and the configured endpoint. server/formalizers.mjs starts a CPU llama-server per selected GGUF on demand (-ngl 0, CUDA hidden, <=8 threads, -np 1, -c 8192, --jinja), reuses it, stops it after 15 idle minutes, runs at most 2 and stops all on exit. The request is lib/formalizer-endpoint.mjs, now shared with tools/research/predict-endpoint.mjs (message only, greedy, the checkpoint's template, no extra stop strings). The chat page has a Model list (localStorage, state 'starting…'/'ready') and an Answer language list: English, Română, Any (auto = the existing request detector). API: model (registry id, 400 unknown_model), language en|ro|auto, POST /v1/models/<id>/start, per-model states on /v1/models and /readyz, formalizer_model/formalizer_label/formalization_ms in the trace, 422 model_output_rejected with the model SOP when the output is not admitted or not executable. Live check on a spare port: 3 messages (EN, RO, mixed) per model all returned SOP; 8/9 answered, Gemma's mixed message selected an unbound variable and returned 422 with its SOP; forced en/ro and auto behave as specified; at most 2 servers ran; all stopped on SIGINT. Tests: tests/formalizers.test.mjs (fake llama-server stub).

author: chat-modes-agent
title: Chat modes (Chat, Formalize, Translate) and syntax keywords in the SOP highlighter
body:
**Chat modes.** The chat page has a Mode selector: *Chat* (plain multi-turn conversation with the unmodified base instruct models SmolLM2-135M-Instruct, SmolLM2-360M-Instruct, Gemma 3 270M-it; temperature 0.7, top_p 0.9, 512-token cap, history kept in server memory per conversation, "Answer in English/Romanian" system instruction when the language is set), *Formalize (SOP Lang)* (unchanged path, fine-tuned formalizers only, message-only prompt), *Translate to English* (base model, fixed prompt as system turn, greedy). `config/formalizers.json` entries carry `capabilities` (`chat`, `translate`, `formalize`) plus per-mode `defaults`; the model list is filtered by mode. Base GGUFs: `models/<model>/chat-base/q8_0.gguf` (copied from the translation experiment's documented base conversions, sha256 in `provenance.json`; no local torch to reconvert). Max running llama-servers raised to 3. API `mode` field (400 `unsupported_mode`); traces show mode, model, latency.

**Highlighter.** `end`, `match`, `all`, `any` (and `not`) are grammar words read from `sop/conditions.mjs`/`sop/parser.mjs`, rendered as syntax keywords linked to `docs/wire_typs/syntax.html#syntax-<word>`; the old renderer did not count `match` blocks, so the final `end` of a `where` group was shown as an undocumented field. Match-block keyword lines now link to the `stated` field definitions.

**Live check (port 9311, scratch state):** Chat: all three base models answered "capital of France" and a follow-up "And of Italy?" correctly using history (75–231 ms). Translate: poor — Gemma and SmolLM2-135M returned the Romanian message unchanged, SmolLM2-360M paraphrased wrongly ("Maria Popescu was born in 2021"); system vs user-turn layouts made no real difference. Formalize: all three fine-tuned models produced the same valid query for "Who works at Alpha Lab?" (0.7–1.3 s). At most 3 servers ran; all stopped.

**Tests:** `tests/sop-code-syntax.test.mjs`, new cases in `tests/formalizers.test.mjs` (fake llama-server). `npm test`: 600/604, the 4 failures are outside this change (status/experiments.json category of another agent's in-progress record; tests/sentence-split.test.mjs). check-links 0 broken, site-menu --check ok, vocabulary check (docs) PASS.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: Two concurrent agent instances both assigned textToCleanEnglish (chat UI + service); reconcile needed
body: This session (actor clean-english-ui-agent) was assigned: survey candidate backends, build lib/text-to-clean-english/, wire the chat UI, update docs. Partway through the preregistered survey (see topic translation), discovered a second live agent instance -- sharing the same actor id in the journal (event at 2026-09-30T05:41:31Z 'textToCleanEnglish: survey, service, UI') plus a related process under actor clean-english-agent -- already building the real deliverable: lib/text-to-clean-english/{index,diff,gate}.mjs and backends/{languagetool,llm,spellfix,symbolic,passthrough}.mjs, config/text-to-clean-english.json (backends.english=languagetool, backends.nonEnglish=llm, LanguageTool actually running on 127.0.0.1:8081), tests/text-to-clean-english.test.mjs, and a larger evaluation tools/research/text-to-clean-english-eval.mjs actively running (GPU+CPU) at the time of writing. Also: this session's own new eval script briefly and accidentally reused the filename of an unrelated, untracked, in-flight script tools/research/clean-english-eval.mjs (experiment eval-clean-english-v1, a dropped v1.5 clean-English training-corpus check, actor clean-english-agent); on inspection the file had its original content and no lasting damage was found, and this session's own generated files were moved out to eval/reports/current/text-to-clean-english-ui-survey/ to stop polluting that unrelated experiment's output directory. Given AGENTS.md's rule against concurrent GPU jobs and unnecessary file races on this shared, non-isolated working tree, this session stopped short of building a second copy of the service/config/tests/UI wiring and closed its own survey early (status/experiments.json text-to-clean-english-v1, journal event state blocked). The owner or orchestrator should pick one instance's lib/text-to-clean-english/, config and tests to keep, and check whether that instance also completed the chat-UI wiring and docs (DS012, DS021, docs/runtime.html, docs/wiki.html, dependencies.md, DS014) that this session did not attempt to avoid duplicating.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: textToCleanEnglish: concurrent build in progress, independent cross-check survey
body:
This session was asked to do the full textToCleanEnglish task (survey, service, chat UI, docs). Partway through an independent stage-1 candidate survey (120 rows: 40 ro + 40 mixed + 40 noisy_en from datasets/formalizer-v1 dev, seed 20260930), discovered that another live concurrent agent instance (same actor id clean-english-ui-agent, journal 2026-09-30T05:44-05:56Z) had already stood down once from duplicating this work, and that a further, still-active agent instance is building the real deliverable in real time: lib/text-to-clean-english/{index,gate,diff?}.mjs + backends/{languagetool,llm}.mjs, config/text-to-clean-english.json, tests/text-to-clean-english.test.mjs, server/http.mjs POST /v1/text-to-clean-english wiring, server/pages/chat.mjs review UI (Accept/Edit/Send original with a word-level diff), DS012/DS021 doc updates and a larger evaluation (tools/research/text-to-clean-english-eval.mjs, LanguageTool running locally on Java 17). File mtimes on lib/text-to-clean-english/index.mjs, gate.mjs and server/http.mjs advanced by minutes during this session's own inspection, confirming the other instance is actively editing right now.

Because of this, this session stood down from writing to any of those files (avoiding the exact file-race pattern the previous standing-down instance flagged) and instead: (1) ran its own independent stage-1 GPU survey as a cross-check, (2) ran `npm test` once and observed a transient failure (24/681 tests, concentrated in tests/formalizers.test.mjs, tests/server-http.test.mjs and every test that imports the chat/admin HTTP surface) caused by server/http.mjs importing `createTextToCleanEnglish`/`decide` from lib/text-to-clean-english/index.mjs, which at that instant only exported `textToCleanEnglish`/`diffWords`/`gate` -- a mid-refactor API mismatch, not a design flaw; the other instance appears to be actively renaming/restructuring the module's public surface (index.mjs and gate.mjs both changed mtime again seconds later, and config/text-to-clean-english.json appeared during this session's inspection). This session did not attempt to fix it, to avoid colliding with that in-flight edit.

Independent cross-check results (heuristic + SymbolicLM-based, GPU EuroLLM-1.7B-Instruct/Qwen3-1.7B/Gemma-3-1b-it via training/python/proofread_llm.py with a new combined proofread+translate+simplify prompt, LanguageTool 6.6 LGPL downloaded standalone + a portable Temurin 17 JRE since only Java 8 was installed): warm per-request latency well inside the 2s UI budget for all three LLMs (0.3-2.1s) and for LanguageTool (about 60ms warm, ~2.6s cold); EuroLLM-1.7B sometimes turns a Romanian yes/no question into an assertion (added "Yes," and dropped the question), a meaning-changing hallucination not seen from Qwen3-1.7B in the same spot-check; SymbolicLM+compareWires scoring of the 120-row sample (direct route, EN parse of the LLM output vs the row's gold SOP) gave mean tolerant wire-F1 0.33 for the untouched original message (baseline) vs 0.28 for EuroLLM-1.7B's cleaned output, with EuroLLM's output identified as all-English 93% of the time (vs 38% for the untouched originals, expected since most originals are Romanian/mixed) -- i.e. EuroLLM trades some execution-relevant meaning for fluency, consistent with the other survey's independent finding (status/experiments.json text-to-clean-english-v1) that both LLM candidates reach higher English fluency than the symbolic/LanguageTool path at a real cost to meaning preservation. This supports defaulting to the symbolic/LanguageTool-first design already being built, with an LLM as an escalation rather than the default for Romanian/mixed.

Recommendation to the orchestrator: reconcile the multiple concurrent clean-english-ui-agent-labeled instances (at least three have now run in this session: this one, the one that stood down at 05:56Z, and the one currently mid-edit), let the currently-active one finish and re-run npm test once its edit settles, and avoid spawning further duplicates of this task.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: textToCleanEnglish library finished and verified end to end
body: lib/text-to-clean-english/ now matches the DS012/DS021-documented contract precisely: textToCleanEnglish(message, options) is a plain async function reading config/text-to-clean-english.json (enabled, backends.english/backends.nonEnglish: languagetool|llm|none), running gate.mjs's cheap LanguagesUtil-only check (non-English tokens, a spelling signal, a handful of grammar-trouble regexes -- no backend call for already-clean English), then calling the chosen backend and returning {original, clean, changed, reasons, spans, backend, confidence}. Both real backends (languagetool.mjs, llm.mjs) mask names/quoted spans/numbers with lib/ud-to-sop/protect.mjs before calling an external server or model and restore them after, because unmasked LanguageTool measurably corrupts unknown proper names (Ungureanu->Unguent, Vlădescu->Blades, Wanjiru Odhiambo->Wanting Huambo -- confirmed independently by this session and by a sibling session's own control-set run). A missing or unreachable backend throws Error with .code='backend_unavailable', which server/http.mjs's POST /v1/text-to-clean-english catches and degrades to backend:'none' rather than failing the chat request. tests/text-to-clean-english.test.mjs (18 tests) mocks fetch and stubs LanguagesUtil resources, so it needs no network, Java or Python and runs in well under a second. A live smoke test against a real LanguageTool 6.6 server (own port, own state dir) confirmed the whole path end to end.

author: chat-backend-agent
title: LanguageProofingLLM is now the textToCleanEnglish backend
body: Qwen3-1.7B removed from the chat registry (GGUF kept). Registry entry language-proofing-llm (capability proofread) serves the fine-tuned Gemma 3 270M it1; message-only bare-sentence prompt, one request per sentence; llm.sendAll (default false) sends clean sentences too; LanguageTool optional, off. Checked live on port 19123 with headless Chromium: Romanian (9 s including model start), mixed and noisy English show the diff with Accept/Edit/Send original at 1100 px and 390 px without horizontal overflow; clean English passes through. Observation: the gate's spelling signal is weak, so 'who is teh boss' and 'when dose Maria start' were not flagged by default; with sendAll true the model fixed both and left a clean sentence unchanged. Per-sentence gating also means a lowercase typo sentence next to a flagged one stays untouched.

author: chat-cnl-agent
title: Chat understanding panel and settings wired (manual-test build)
body: SymbolicLM service now reports analysis, rewrite trace and the per-sentence interpretation (round trip via SymbolicLM, certification via both Stanza packages) on request; chat server relays it as chatSop.understanding and starts symbolic-proofing-llm on demand for gated/always. Browser check, five messages, 1280 and 390 px, no overflow: clean English verified+certified; tangled English rewrite accepted (certified) with the original and rewrite shown; Romanian and mixed go through LanguageProofingLLM review then verified CNL; 'not counting Csaba' shown as not represented, highlighted in the message, rewrite rejected, not certified. One bug found by the browser check and fixed (badge title on an appended node). The rewrite default stays off: a mid-task coordinator message asking for gated-by-default, Q-PROOF-1 removal and a separate leftover-span list was blocked by the permission system and is left undone.

author: api-agent
title: Capability APIs, version-keyed caches and the independent chat flow
body: Five endpoints (proofread, understand, symbolic rewrite/analyze, emotion detect) plus capabilities and admin cache stats, each answer with status/errors/timings/cache/versions; analysis never fails totally (partial status, failed sentence rows, clarify). lib/cache/lru.mjs: LRU by entries and bytes, TTL, in-flight dedup, failures not cached; caches in front of every model call and the SymbolicLM analysis and inside the service (Stanza parse, certification, rewrite). Measured on real models, private port: formalize of an unseen message 842-1020 ms vs 6-8 ms after understand+emotion of the same message; repeated calls 2-3 ms. Decision: emotion detection moved from the SymbolicLM service to the host (service always called with emotion false) so the independent emotion API and the formalize request share one cache. DS030 holds the contract.

author: owner
title: Coding-agent path, base memories and sessions; UD-to-SOP query rules priority
body: Owner 2026-10-01 (chat, condensed verbatim parts): (1) priority work stream: translation from the grammatical analysis into SOP Lang for queries (rules/heuristics from UD to wires, also more advanced wires), no GPU needed; (2) complex inputs or attached instruction files, or detected failures, go to a coding agent (omp with the new authoring skill) instead of SymbolicLM; a setting to always do this if omp is configured with DeepSeek or a subscription; a skill to call omp with a temporary folder; an API listing the models available in omp; requests create temporary folders; (3) sessions get temporary folders where the base memory is cloned and new circuits are added during the conversation; the chat UI gets the concept of base memory: choose the base memory version when starting a session, fork a base memory (choosing its memory strategy) and add knowledge; old chat discussions and databases may be dropped; a gitignored root folder for chat data; 'Pune un sonet sa faca astea, e un task mare, explica-i pas cu pas si fa-i review, teste'; update DS and HTML docs and the chat UI; (4) Stanza agents use the GPU when it is free. Transcribed by the orchestrator.

author: perf-agent
title: Why the chat check was slow, and the fix
body: Cause measured on port 19611: maxRunning 3 against up to four pipeline processes, so a Romanian then an English sentence stopped and started prod1 and the translator (each 2-3 s), and the first message paid the whole cold start (word lists 13 s, SymbolicLM 25 s). Baseline: cold Hello 56.7 s, Romanian 15.3 s, English with typos 8.2 s. After (warm, host load 14-16): Hello 0.66 s then about 20 ms, English 1.0-1.3 s, Romanian 1.9-3.8 s, zero starts or evictions after the 22-28 s background warmup. Remaining cost is SymbolicLM compute (Stanza parse plus interpretation round trip) and a 6-13 s synchronous word-list read at start.
